info.name: Arena Exit
info.text: The way out, with a bucket for the faint of stomach. It is emptied after every fight, and it is never empty.

info.name: Arena Entrance
info.text: The ticket hut, skull on the roof. Seats are numbered, limbs are not.

info.name: Arena
info.text: A round sand pit with a stone ring and three rows of planks. Men walk in through the gate; how many walk out is up to the gods and the crowd.

info.name: Sand Pit
info.text: The first arena: a ring of planks around a pit of sand, a lanista's box and two sails for the nobility. The sand is raked every morning; the stains stay anyway.

info.name: Acacia
info.text: A flat-topped acacia, the only shade for a day in any direction. Lions, vultures and travellers all agree on that, and they rarely agree on anything else.

info.name: Apple Tree
info.text: Red apples, free for the taking. The worms were here first and they are not sharing.

info.name: Baobab
info.text: A baobab with a trunk like a wine jar. Hollow inside, which the locals use for storing water, grain and the occasional tax collector.

info.name: Birch
info.text: A pale birch. Its rods are flexible, cheap and well remembered by every recruit.

info.name: Beech
info.text: A broad beech with a smooth grey trunk. Burns long and hot, which the smith appreciates more than the beech does.

info.name: Date Palm
info.text: A tall palm heavy with dates. Sweet enough for a senator, and the climb is steep enough to cull the greedy.

info.name: Old Oak
info.text: An oak older than the empire and twice as honest. Its roots have drunk from more battlefields than any legionary. Excellent shade, terrible witness.

info.name: Tree Fern
info.text: A fern grown tall enough to call itself a tree. It was old when the gods were young and has not been impressed since.

info.name: Coconut Palm
info.text: A leaning palm with a crown of coconuts. Every year it drops one on somebody, and every year the priests call it a sign.

info.name: Liana Tree
info.text: A jungle tree hung with lianas. Good for swinging, better for hanging, and nobody here ever bothers to tell the two apart.

info.name: Mangrove
info.text: A mangrove standing on its roots in the brine. The crabs live underneath, the mosquitoes above, and lost sandals in between.

info.name: Olive Tree
info.text: A gnarled olive tree, older than the oldest grudge in town. Oil for the lamps, oil for the wounds, oil for the bribes.

info.name: Poplar
info.text: A tall, thin poplar. Soft wood, fast growth and no character at all, rather like a senator.

info.name: Fir
info.text: A dark fir, straight as a spear. Makes good beams, good masts and, if business is slow, good coffins.

info.name: Cypress
info.text: A slim dark cypress, the traditional tree of graveyards. It grows near the arena for the same reason.

info.name: Straw Bed
info.text: A wooden frame, old straw and one blanket. The fleas were here first and they pay no rent either.

info.name: Ploughed Field
info.text: Furrows of dark earth with green shoots. Somebody sweated here so somebody else can eat in the stands.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Floor
info.text: Stamped clay with straw in it. Spill something and it becomes part of the floor.

info.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Right
info.text: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.

info.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Front
info.text: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.

info.name: Thatch Front A
info.text: Same straw, a hole the size of a fist. Something small is already moving in.

info.name: Thatch Front B
info.text: Same straw, a little more rot on the north side. Nobody has noticed. Nobody looks up.

info.name: Thatch Front C
info.text: Same straw, wearing its moss like a bad toupee.

info.name: Thatch Front D
info.text: The roof gave way here. The crow took the opportunity and has not left since.

info.name: Thatch Front E
info.text: Stripped to the laths. Someone ate the thatch. Someone else ate that someone.

info.name: Thatch Front F
info.text: Blood runs down the straw. The roofer fell, the roof held. Priorities.

info.name: Thatch Front Ridge
info.text: The ridge. Straw sticks up like a cheap wig; the wind has opinions about it.

info.name: Thatch Front Eave A
info.text: A ragged eave. It sheds rain, mostly onto whoever stands under it.

info.name: Thatch Front Eave B
info.text: A crooked eave, one handspan too short. The roofer ran out of straw and patience.

info.name: Thatch Front Eave C

info.name: Thatched Roof, Flat
info.text: A flat bed of thatch. Good for drying fish and hiding from tax men.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Window
info.text: A hole in the wall with a straw mat for a curtain. Keeps out the light, lets in the flies.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Window A
info.text: Boarded up from inside. Someone counted the days on the wall below. Then they stopped counting.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Window B
info.text: Dried fish on a string, and a rat nobody admits to. Dinner hangs where everyone can see it.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Window D
info.text: The shutter hangs by one hinge and the scratches below go the wrong way. Nobody asks who wanted out.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable
info.text: Boards nailed up under the end of the roof. They hold, mostly.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable A
info.text: Cracked clay between old timber rails. The repair is cheaper than admitting the roof is falling.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (down)
info.text: The other half of the timber gable. Nobody remembers which half was built first.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (up)
info.text: The pointed end of a timber gable. The birds nest here and pay no rent.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Tiers
info.text: Rows of plank benches. Splinters are free and so is the view of the killing.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Sign
info.text: A crooked board on a stick with a daub of paint. Nobody can read, so a picture of a sausage does the job.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Door
info.text: A plank door that sticks in summer and in winter. In spring it merely creaks.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall
info.text: Clay packed over a timber frame. Cracks come free of charge, draughts are included.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall A
info.text: A fresh daub of clay over last winter's hole. Still damp, still lumpy, still cheaper than a mason.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall B
info.text: A crack wide enough to post letters through. The straw inside is the only thing holding it together.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall D
info.text: A rat nailed up by its tail. Pest control, warning and decoration in one.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Upper Wall
info.text: An upper floor of clay on a crooked frame. The brace is the only straight thing in the house.

info.name: Mud-and-Timber Upper Wall A
info.text: A bird nests under the beam and pays its rent on the wall below.

info.name: Marble Floor
info.text: Marble slabs with a purple inlay. Slippery when wet, and it is always wet with something.

info.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Right
info.text: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.

info.name: Marble Slab Right A
info.text: Pigeons have discovered marble. It is the only luxury they share with the owner.

info.name: Marble Slab Right D
info.text: A cracked slab. Marble is hard, but a falling tenant is harder.

info.name: Marble Window
info.text: A tall window with a bronze grille and a little gilded pediment. Bars, but tasteful ones.

info.name: Marble Gable
info.text: A marble gable, straight as a senator claims to be.

info.name: Marble Gable Peak (down)
info.text: The other gilded pediment edge. Symmetry costs extra and the owner paid.

info.name: Marble Gable Peak (up)
info.text: A gilded pediment edge. The gods look down from here, the owner looks down on everyone else.

info.name: Marble Tiers
info.text: White marble tiers for people who never sit on anything cheaper. The blood looks better from here.

info.name: Marble Sign
info.text: A bronze plaque on a marble pedestal. Whatever it advertises, you cannot afford it.

info.name: Marble Door
info.text: A bronze door with gilded studs. Heavy enough to keep out the mob and, on a good day, the creditors.

info.name: Marble Wall
info.text: Polished marble with a gilded band, paid for with somebody else's blood. Marble always is.

info.name: Marble Wall A
info.text: A crack filled with gilded putty. Patched like the reputation of the man who paid for it.

info.name: Marble Wall B
info.text: A donor's inscription, half chiselled away. He fell from favour; the wall only fell halfway.

info.name: Marble Wall D
info.text: Something red runs down from the gilded band. The owner insists it is wine. It is always wine.

info.name: Marble Upper Wall
info.text: An upper floor of polished marble. Up here the screams from the street arrive slightly muffled.

info.name: Pantile Right
info.text: Curved terracotta tiles, cap over channel. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.

info.name: Pantile Right A
info.text: Sun-bleached tiles among the red. The roofer swears they are all from the same kiln.

info.name: Pantile Right B
info.text: Mismatched tiles from three demolished houses. Recycling, the landlord calls it.

info.name: Pantile Right C
info.text: Yellow lichen on old tiles. It has outlived four owners.

info.name: Pantile Right D
info.text: A broken tile and a hole beneath. The rain gets the bedroom, the rats get the rest.

info.name: Pantile Right E
info.text: Stones weighing down loose tiles. Cheaper than nails and good for throwing at tax men.

info.name: Pantile Right F

info.name: Whitewash Window
info.text: An upper window with green shutters. From up here you can see the arena and smell the tannery.

info.name: Whitewash Window A
info.text: Shutters closed tight, with a knothole at eye height. Someone up there is always watching.

info.name: Whitewash Window B
info.text: A pot of herbs on the sill. Dead since the last drought, still watered out of spite.

info.name: Whitewash Window C
info.text: Laundry on a line: a tunic, a loincloth, a rag of uncertain purpose. Nothing here is ever really clean.

info.name: Whitewash Window D
info.text: A birdcage on a nail. The bird stopped singing some time ago. Nobody noticed which day.

info.name: Whitewash Window E
info.text: A chamber pot on the sill, freshly emptied downwards. Look up before you walk below.

info.name: Whitewash Gable
info.text: A whitewashed gable. Pigeons rent it by the day.

info.name: Whitewash Gable A
info.text: A whitewashed gable with a dove hole. The doves are dinner, the droppings are décor.

info.name: Whitewash Gable Peak (down)
info.text: The falling verge, finished with a row of clay tiles. Rain runs straight into the neighbour's window.

info.name: Whitewash Gable Peak (up)
info.text: The rising verge, finished with a row of clay tiles. Wind gets in anyway.

info.name: Whitewash Gable B
info.text: A gable with a dove hole and the evidence running down from it.

info.name: Whitewash Door
info.text: An arched door of rough planks with iron studs. The studs are for the bailiff.

info.name: Whitewash Door A
info.text: The door stands ajar. Either they trust the street or there is nothing left to steal.

info.name: Whitewash Door B
info.text: A red curtain instead of a door. Cheaper than wood and just as useless against thieves.

info.name: Whitewash Wall
info.text: Whitewash over cheap brick on an ochre plinth. Every spring a fresh coat, every autumn fresh stains.

info.name: Whitewash Wall A
info.text: A window with blue shutters, so the neighbours can watch the executions without paying.

info.name: Whitewash Wall B
info.text: The plaster has given up here. The bricks underneath are no better.

info.name: Whitewash Wall C
info.text: A small window and an iron ring for tethering a donkey, a goat or a debtor.

info.name: Whitewash Wall D
info.text: A crack and a wanted poster, already crossed out. The reward went to whoever brought the head.

info.name: Whitewash Wall E
info.text: A bloody handprint by the door. Someone was looking for the medicus and found the wall.

info.name: Whitewash Wall F
info.text: A wall shrine to Grumulus, god of locked doors. Someone stole his head; he never saw it coming.

info.name: Whitewash Upper Wall
info.text: Plain whitewash on the upper floor. Up here the stains are older and the rent is lower.

info.name: Whitewash Upper Wall A
info.text: A small vent slit. It lets out the smoke and lets in the screams from the arena.

info.name: Whitewash Upper Wall B
info.text: Scaffold holes and a damp streak. The builders left in a hurry, the damp never left.

info.name: Whitewash Upper Wall C
info.text: A patch of fresh plaster over an old crack. Nobody asks what was behind it.

info.name: Brick Floor
info.text: Terracotta tiles, red and buff. They hide wine stains well and blood even better.

info.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Right
info.text: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.

info.name: Tiled Right A
info.text: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.

info.name: Tiled Right D
info.text: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.

info.name: Brick Window
info.text: A window in a brick frame with green shutters. Ideal for emptying pots onto passers-by.

info.name: Brick Gable
info.text: A plastered gable wall. Pigeons rent it by the day.

info.name: Brick Gable Peak (down)
info.text: The falling half of a plastered gable. Rain runs down it and into the neighbour's window.

info.name: Brick Gable Peak (up)
info.text: The peak of a plastered gable. The highest point of the house and of the landlord's ambitions.

info.name: Brick Tiers
info.text: Tiers of stone seats. Bring a cushion, or rent one at a price that hurts more than the stone.

info.name: Brick Sign
info.text: A painted signboard with a red frame. It promises quality and is right about half the time.

info.name: Brick Door
info.text: A wooden door under a brick lintel. Knock twice; the third knock is always the debt collector.

info.name: Brick Wall
info.text: Plastered brick on a red plinth. Respectable enough to have debts.

info.name: Brick Wall A
info.text: The plaster has let go and the bricks show through. The landlord calls it rustic charm.

info.name: Brick Wall B
info.text: A list of names scratched in charcoal, each with a tally. Not a guest list. Nobody on it is invited anywhere.

info.name: Brick Wall D
info.text: A bloody handprint at shoulder height. Someone leaned here on the way out of a dispute.

info.name: Brick Upper Wall
info.text: An upper floor of plastered brick. The higher the floor, the cheaper the tenant and the longer the fall.

info.name: Thistle
info.text: A thistle with a purple crown. It stabs everyone who touches it and has never lost a fight.

info.name: Tall Grass
info.text: Grass up to the hip, dry and golden. Whatever hunts in it can see you long before you see it.

info.name: Reeds
info.text: Reeds at the edge of the water. Good for roofs, baskets and for losing a sandal.

info.name: Wildflowers
info.text: A handful of wildflowers. Pretty, harmless and trampled within the week.

info.name: Bare Earth
info.text: Honest dirt with a few pebbles. Everything you own will end up in it, and so will you.

info.name: Bedrock
info.text: Solid rock. Nothing grows here and nothing can be buried here, which makes it popular with neither farmers nor undertakers.

info.name: River
info.text: Brown in the cities, blue on the maps. Downstream, everyone drinks what upstream washed off.

info.name: River (current)
info.text: Swift, cold and in a hurry, like a debtor who just saw the gate open.

info.name: River (foam)
info.text: The froth is natural. Mostly. The tanners say so, and they should know.

info.name: River (drifting barrel)
info.text: A barrel heading downstream. Wine, nails or a tax collector; nobody fishes it out to check.

info.name: River (dead rat)
info.text: Belly up and still the best swimmer in the city.

info.name: Grass
info.text: Grass. It grows on anything, including last season's losers.

info.name: Sand
info.text: Fine sand, excellent at soaking up whatever gets spilled on it. The arena uses the same kind, for the same reason.

info.name: Waterhole
info.text: Fresh water, more or less. The men drink from it, the oxen stand in it, and nobody asks in which order.

info.name: Dirt Road
info.text: Packed earth with two cart ruts. Carts love it; whoever falls asleep on it will not love the carts.

info.name: Banana Plant
info.text: A banana plant with a hand of yellow fruit. The monkeys took the ripe ones and left you the bill.

info.name: Flowering Bush
info.text: A bush with orange blossoms. The bees adore it; the men use it for something less poetic.

info.name: Bush
info.text: A plain green bush. Just big enough to hide a coward, as several have already discovered.

info.name: Hazel
info.text: A hazel shrub. Nuts in autumn, switches all year round.

info.name: Tamarisk
info.text: A pale tamarisk that drinks the ground dry. Thrives where everything else gives up, which makes it the patron shrub of debtors.

info.name: Tiled Roof
info.text: Red clay tiles over a plastered gable. Keeps the rain off the men and the men out of sight.

info.name: Boulder
info.text: A grey boulder that has not moved since the gods dropped it. Patient, silent and completely useless until someone brings a pickaxe.

info.name: Rock Terrace
info.text: The hill under the important people. It holds them up better than the people below do.

info.name: Rock Terrace
info.text: Bare rock, one step higher. Down here you pay rent, up there you collect it.

info.name: Rock Stairs
info.text: Cut into the hill by convicts, worn smooth by priests, slippery for everybody else.

info.name: Worker
info.text: An ordinary man of the ludus in a simple tunic. He carries, saws and digs until the day somebody hands him a sword instead.

info.name: Ox Cart
info.text: A cart with one ox and three sacks. The ox does the work and the driver takes the credit; the ox is used to it.

info.name: Storage Spot
info.text: A pallet with crates and a sack. Everything here belongs to somebody, and that somebody is not the man carrying it.

info.name: Storage Spot A
info.text: Two barrels and a crate. One holds wine, one holds vinegar, and the label fell off years ago.

info.name: Storage Spot B
info.text: Grain sacks and an amphora. The weevils got here first and are not paying rent.

info.name: Storage Spot C
info.text: Firewood stacked by someone who will never be warm.

info.name: Storage Spot D
info.text: A crate of skulls, sorted by size. The arena sells everything, eventually.

info.name: Storage Spot E
info.text: Spare chains and a sack of grain with a rat on top. The rat lost the negotiation.

info.name: Corpse
info.text: A fallen gladiator in a dark puddle. He lies here for a day so the next ones know what the purse costs; then the cart takes him.

info.name: Slave Market
info.text: The slave trader's stall. Every morning he brings five new men in chains; whoever is left at dusk goes back on the road with him. No refunds.

info.name: Wall Walk
info.text: Wide enough for two soldiers, or one soldier and his excuses.

info.name: Wall Crown Half W
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Wall Crown Half N
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Slanted Wall
info.text: The wall turns a corner here. Attackers do too, mostly into the moat.

info.name: Slanted Wall A
info.text: A crack the size of a bribe. The mason swears it is decorative.

info.name: Slanted Wall B
info.text: The new stone is where someone was thrown through the old one.

info.name: Slanted Wall C
info.text: Same stones, different order. The masons got paid by the layer.

info.name: Slanted Wall D
info.text: Built in a hurry the year the barbarians were rumoured. They never came. The wall stayed crooked.

info.name: Slanted Battlements W
info.text: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.

info.name: Slanted Battlements
info.text: Battlements on a bend, for archers who like a view of the whole crowd.

info.name: Slanted Battlements A
info.text: One merlon gave up. So did the guard behind it.

info.name: Slanted Battlements B
info.text: The arrow is a souvenir. The stain is the previous owner of the souvenir.

info.text: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.

info.name: Slanted Battlements Back
info.text: The back of the battlements. Nobody looks at it except the guards, who look at nothing.

info.name: Town Wall
info.text: Built to keep the barbarians out. Mostly keeps the taxpayers in.

info.name: Town Wall
info.text: Every stone paid for twice: once by the city, once more into the mayor's villa.

info.name: Wall Ramp
info.text: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.

info.name: Medicus
info.text: A small house with a slate roof and the staff of Asclepius over the door. The medicus sews, sets and saws for gold; the cheaper the treatment, the longer the scream.

info.name: Tree Stump
info.text: What is left of a tree after the woodcutter has been by. Give it a few days and it will try again; trees never learn.

info.name: Closed Sign
info.text: A plank on a stick: CLOSED. The crowd reads it, sighs, and goes into town to watch a hanging instead.

info.name: Wooden Jetty
info.text: Planks on stilts above the water. Each board has been walked on by a sailor, a fishwife and at least one fool who jumped.

info.text: Sandals so good you could flee a lion in them. Almost.

info.name: Coffin Maker
info.text: One size fits all, if you fold them.

info.name: Cooper
info.text: Every barrel holds wine or a secret. Usually both.

info.name: Copper Mine
info.text: Green rock, red hands.

info.name: Cottage
info.text: Has a door. Locals call it luxury.

info.name: Courier Post
info.text: Swift horses, slow excuses.

info.name: Selene's Creeper Bower
info.text: Pretty flowers. Do not sniff them. Everybody sniffs them.

info.name: Dairy
info.text: Milk, aged until it fights back.

info.name: Domus
info.text: Atrium, fountain, an ancestor mask that judges you.

info.name: Dormouse Jar Farm
info.text: Fattened in jars, served with honey, mourned by no one.

info.name: Dust Grinder
info.text: Grinds stone into courage. Side effects: everything.

info.name: Dye Garden
info.text: Red for the home team, blue for the corpses.

info.name: Dyer's Vats
info.text: The river is red today. Probably the dye.
info.plan: Cloth, Madder, Woad, Water → Dyed Cloth

info.name: Glutton's Kitchen
info.text: If it walked, flew or lost in the arena, it's on the menu.
info.plan: Dormice, Peacocks, Oysters, Mushrooms, Saffron, Tiere aus der Arena → Exotic Dishes

info.name: Fence's Cellar
info.text: Everything is legal if nobody saw it.

info.name: Fighting Pit
info.text: Small pit, big dreams, short careers.

info.name: Firewood Yard
info.text: Turns trees into warmth and splinters into sons.

info.name: Fisherman's Hut
info.text: Catches fish, tells lies.

info.name: Flax Farm
info.text: Grows bandages, eventually.

info.name: Flower Garden
info.text: Petals for winners, wreaths for the rest.

info.name: Fodder Store
info.text: The lions eat better than the plebs. Fewer complaints.

info.name: Forester
info.text: Plants trees for men who will cut them. A tragic profession.

info.name: Fortune Teller
info.text: Predicts the winner. Refunds never.

info.name: Forum
info.text: Free speech, paid listening.

info.name: Furrier
info.text: Fashion that once had a face.

info.name: Fish Sauce Vats
info.text: Rotten fish sauce. The rich pay double for it.

info.name: Glassworks
info.text: Breath of fire, fragile results. Like a love affair.

info.name: Goat Pen
info.text: Climbs everything except the social ladder.

info.name: Goldsmith
info.text: Makes the rich shine and the poor squint.
info.plan: Gold Dust, Silver Bars → Gold Bars, Jewellery, Victor's Wreath

info.name: Gold Panner
info.text: Sifts mud for glory. Finds mostly mud.

info.name: Gorgon Quarry
info.text: The rock stares back. The workers stop blinking.

info.name: Governor's Palace
info.text: Rules the province from a very soft chair.

info.name: Granary
info.text: Rats' paradise. Cats' workplace.

info.name: Guildhall
info.text: Where tradesmen agree to overcharge together.

info.name: Harbour
info.text: Ships bring silk, pepper and plague. Two are taxable.

info.name: Quack Doctor
info.text: Cures everything except what you have.

info.name: Hemp Farm
info.text: For rope. Only rope. Stop asking.

info.name: Hydra Reed Bed
info.text: Cut one reed, two grow back. Nobody complains.

info.name: Incense Maker
info.text: Makes the gods happy and the priests dizzy.

info.name: Infirmary
info.text: Patches up the brave. Bills the dead.

info.name: Roadside Inn
info.text: Clean sheets every month, whether you need them or not.

info.name: Iron Mine
info.text: Dark, deep and dangerous. The pay is too.

info.name: Kennels
info.text: Good boys, bad intentions.

info.name: Latrine
info.text: Twelve seats, no walls, great conversations.

info.name: Lavender Field
info.text: Makes the rich smell less like the poor.

info.name: Lethe Spring
info.text: Drink once and forget the bill. The landlord does not.

info.name: Lime Kiln
info.text: Burns rocks. Don't ask what else.

info.name: Malthouse
info.text: Grain that drank too much.

info.name: Marble Quarry
info.text: White, cold, expensive. Like a senator.

info.name: Market Square
info.text: Everything for sale, especially the truth.
info.plan: Pflicht in jedem Ort (5.1): Mitte des Orts, Anfang des Wegenetzes, verteilt Waren an Wohnhäuser, Handel mit Fremden

info.name: Market Garden
info.text: Cabbages. The vegetable nobody throws a party for.

info.name: Stonemason
info.text: Carves your name in stone. Spelling extra.

info.name: Oil & Massage
info.text: Rubs out knots and memories.

info.name: Meadery
info.text: Honey wine, for heroes and the very sad.

info.name: Hay Meadow
info.text: Grass, but organised.

info.name: Menagerie
info.text: Look, don't touch. Seriously. Don't.

info.name: Grain Mill
info.text: Grinds grain and the occasional finger.

info.name: Mirror Polisher
info.text: So patricians can admire the only person they love.

info.name: Mortar Yard
info.text: Roman concrete. Will outlive your grandchildren. And you.
info.plan: Lime, Volcanic Ash, Rubble, Water → Concrete

info.name: Murex Pens
info.text: Ten thousand snails die for one purple hem.

info.name: Mushroom Shed
info.text: Dark, damp, delicious. Mostly.

info.name: Oat Farm
info.text: Feeds horses and the poor. In that order.

info.name: Olive Press
info.text: Squeezes olives like taxmen squeeze farmers.

info.name: Olive Grove
info.text: Trees older than the empire, and less corrupt.

info.name: Orchard
info.text: Ripe for eating, overripe for throwing.

info.name: Oyster Bed
info.text: Pearls for the ladies, food poisoning for the gents.

info.name: Portrait Painter
info.text: Paints champions while they're still whole.

info.name: Palazzo
info.text: So many rooms nobody has found the cousin yet.

info.name: Honey Bakery
info.text: Sweet enough to make a senator smile. Once.

info.name: Pawnshop
info.text: We don't ask. You don't tell.
info.plan: gestohlene und verpfändete Waren → billige Waren

info.name: Peacock Garden
info.text: Beautiful, loud, and delicious. Like a tenor.

info.name: Peat Cutter
info.text: Sometimes he finds a fuel, sometimes a very old man.

info.name: Perfumer
info.text: For the nose, when the arena is downwind.

info.name: Petal Booth
info.text: For the winner. The loser gets the sand.

info.name: Physic Garden
info.text: Cures headaches, causes others.

info.name: Pie Shop
info.text: Don't look inside. Just enjoy.

info.name: Pig Farm
info.text: They eat anything. We don't ask what.

info.name: Underground Pit
info.text: First rule: don't mention the lanista.

info.name: Puls Kitchen
info.text: Roman gruel. Grey, warm, eaten without eye contact.

info.name: Posca Stand
info.text: Vinegar water. Soldiers love it. Soldiers love anything.

info.name: Potter
info.text: Shapes clay with love, sells it with lies.
info.plan: Clay, Firewood → Amphorae, Pottery, Oil Lamps, Clay Gladiators

info.name: Prosthetics Workshop
info.text: Wooden legs, hooks and a loyalty discount.

info.name: Public Latrine
info.text: The only seat with no view of the arena. Still full.

info.name: Purple Vats
info.text: Smells like the sea died. It did.

info.name: Quarry
info.text: Rocks, and the men who were sentenced to them.

info.name: Queue Path
info.text: Waiting is half the fun. The other half is dying.

info.name: Racetrack
info.text: Round and round until someone falls off.

info.name: Reed Cutter
info.text: Wet feet, dry humour.

info.name: Tallow Boiler
info.text: Turns leftovers into light and glue. Waste not.

info.name: Resin Tapper
info.text: Bleeds trees. Calls it a craft.

info.name: Rookery King's Hall
info.text: A throne made of stolen chairs.

info.name: Ropewalk
info.text: Long building, short tempers.

info.name: Rotten Fruit Stand
info.text: Ammunition for the opinionated.

info.name: Royal Palace
info.text: Built by thousands, enjoyed by one.

info.name: Saffron Field
info.text: Worth more than the man who picks it.

info.name: Salt Pan
info.text: The sea, minus the sea.

info.name: Sand Pit
info.text: Dig here for sand. Or for whoever owed the Lanista.

info.name: Sand Shed
info.text: Fresh sand daily. Yesterday's is in the garden.
info.plan: Sand, Sawdust → frischer Arenaboden nach jedem Kampf

info.name: Sausage Maker
info.text: What's in it? Love. And other things.

info.name: Sawmill
info.text: Logs in, planks out, fingers optional.

info.name: Grammar School
info.text: Teaches reading, so they can read the betting odds.

info.name: Tablet Maker
info.text: Writes the fight card before the fight. Mostly accurate.
info.plan: Wax, Planks → Writing Tablets, Arena Programmes

info.name: Sculptor
info.text: Makes heroes immortal. Noses fall off first.

info.name: Sea Fishery
info.text: Brave men, small boats, big stories.

info.name: Senate House
info.text: Six hundred men, one opinion: theirs.

info.name: Shack
info.text: Four walls, mostly.

info.name: Sheep Farm
info.text: Count them twice. Somebody's always stealing one.

info.name: Shipyard
info.text: Builds ships. Some even float.

info.name: Shrine
info.text: Leave a coin. The gods take card. Eventually.

info.name: Silk Tailor
info.text: From the far East. Like the price.

info.name: Silver Furnace
info.text: Coins, cups and other reasons to stab someone.

info.name: Silver Mine
info.text: Every vein a bribe waiting to happen.

info.name: Iron Smelter
info.text: Hot enough to melt rock and resolve.

info.name: Smoke Curer
info.text: Cures reeds, not the habit.

info.name: Smokehouse
info.text: Food that survives longer than the soldier.

info.name: Smugglers' Store
info.text: Duty-free. Also conscience-free.

info.name: Soap Maker
info.text: Pig fat and ashes. Still cleaner than you.

info.name: Saffron Spray Tower
info.text: Scented mist, so the rich can't smell the poor.

info.name: Spice House
info.text: Pepper from across the world, for a man who can't taste anymore.
info.plan: Fine Wine, Pepper, Honey → Spiced Wine

info.name: Spinner
info.text: Spins wool and gossip.

info.name: Ox Spit
info.text: Slow-cooked for six hours, eaten in six seconds.

info.name: Spoliarium
info.text: Where the losers go to be paperwork.
info.plan: Tote aus der Arena → Coffins, Tiere → Glutton's Kitchen

info.name: Stable
info.text: Muscle for carts, opinions not included.

info.name: Beer Tent
info.text: Liquid courage, sold by the cup.

info.name: Cushion Rental
info.text: Stone seats, soft profits.

info.name: Glutton's Tent
info.text: Try the lion. He lost earlier.

info.name: Fish on a Stick
info.text: Caught this morning, cooked this afternoon, regretted tonight.

info.name: Pie Stand
info.text: “Mystery meat” is a promise.

info.name: Gruel Cart
info.text: Hot, cheap, and from yesterday.

info.name: Champion Gallery
info.text: Buy him now. He might not be around next week.

info.name: Programme Seller
info.text: Lists who's fighting and who's been crossed off.

info.name: Ox Spit Booth
info.text: Carved fresh, like the fighters.

info.name: Sausage Stall
info.text: Gladiator-shaped. Coincidence.

info.name: Souvenir Stall
info.text: Genuine gladiator sweat. Mostly.
info.plan: Bloodied Rags, Clay Gladiators, Bone Dice

info.name: Water Seller
info.text: Free water costs one coin.

info.name: Wine Stall
info.text: Red to match the sand.

info.name: Extra Stands
info.text: The closer you sit, the more you get to keep.
info.plan: weitere Sitzplätze nach Stufe: Standing, Benches, Seats, Boxes, Imperial Box; die Ränge selbst gehören zur Arena

info.name: Gravestone Carver
info.text: Here lies Marcus. He lost.

info.name: Stud Farm
info.text: Breeds racers. Losers become sausages.

info.name: Sulphur Pit
info.text: The gates of hell, open Tuesday to Saturday.

info.name: Tailor
info.text: Makes you look like a citizen until you speak.
info.plan: Cloth (Wolle), Dyed Cloth, Chalk → Rough Tunic, Cloaks, Toga (gekalkt weiß)

info.name: Tannery
info.text: Smells like death, because it is.

info.name: Tavern
info.text: Where rumours are born, drunk, and sold.

info.name: Tax Office
info.text: Nobody likes them. Everybody pays.

info.name: Tear Press
info.text: Squeezes berries until they confess.

info.name: Temple
info.text: The gods accept goats, gold and public apologies.

info.name: Tenement
info.text: Six floors, one staircase, zero fire exits.

info.name: Theatre
info.text: Like the arena, but the deaths are fake. Boring.

info.name: Tin Mine
info.text: Rare enough to start wars. Small ones.

info.name: Toga Weaver
info.text: Twelve yards of fabric to prove you never work.

info.name: Torch Store
info.text: Night fights: twice the drama, half the visibility.

info.name: Townhouse
info.text: Workshop downstairs, family upstairs, smell everywhere.

info.name: Trading Post
info.text: Buys low, sells high, smiles always.
info.plan: Handel mit einem Ort, eigene Händler

info.name: Training Yard
info.text: Sweat now, bleed later.

info.name: Trapper
info.text: Patient, quiet, missing two fingers.

info.name: Undertaker
info.text: Business is booming. Literally, near the arena.

info.name: Awning Mast
info.text: Shade for the crowd, none for the fighters.
info.plan: Linen, Rope → Sonnensegel (mehr Besucher im Sommer)

info.name: Vice Den
info.text: Come for the smoke, stay because you forgot the way out.

info.name: Vice Tent
info.text: The crowd cheers louder. Nobody remembers why.

info.name: Villa
info.text: Servants included. Gratitude not.

info.name: Vine Drier
info.text: Hangs leaves to dry and customers to wait.

info.name: Vineyard
info.text: Sun, slope and slaves stomping. Two of those are fine.

info.name: Armoury
info.text: Every blade counted. Every missing one blamed on the new guy.

info.name: Warehouse
info.text: Holds everything except the guards' honesty.

info.name: Watch House
info.text: Keeps the peace, sells the leftovers.

info.name: Weaponsmith
info.text: Every blade is tested. On someone.
info.plan: Iron Bars, Planks, Leather → Gladius, Spear, Trident

info.name: Weaver
info.text: Every thread a tiny miracle of boredom.

info.name: Well
info.text: Mostly water. Sometimes bucket.

info.name: Wheat Farm
info.text: Bread starts here, as does back pain.

info.name: Whip Maker
info.text: For beast tamers and motivational speeches.

info.name: Wine Cellar
info.text: Aged twenty years, drunk in twenty minutes.
info.plan: Wine, Amphorae → Fine Wine (reift 10 Spieltage ohne Arbeiter)

info.name: Winepress
info.text: Feet were washed. We think.

info.name: Woodcutter's Hut
info.text: Trees fear him. Squirrels hate him.
